Deputies deal with an angry and aggressive transient; a truck is pulled over by a deputy, and one of the occupants is found to have a felony warrant; a man reports that his wife is beating him, and through a hammer at him.

Deputies respond to a report of an inebriated man trying to change a tire on the side of the road; a report of a suspicious person in the back of a store, loading items onto his truck; a man claims his car broke down at 3:00 a.m.
Deputy Roberts responds to a report of an individual committing a robbery and is a known officer safety threat.

A troubled young man with physical limitations decides to fight with the police; the boat patrol on Lake Tahoe responds to an overturned vessel in the water; a vehicle with an out-of-date registration is pulled over.

Detectives and deputies arrest sex traffickers in a prostitution sting operation; a store owner reports a suspicious man looking into car windows; a deputy is called to a business where four people sitting in a car appear to be up to no good.

A deputy investigates a report of a man strangling a woman; a report of a person screaming obscenities and throwing chairs; a deputy responds to a call for assistance from a department store loss prevention officer.
A deputy responds to a house fire several days before Christmas, and later, plays Santa to some kids who lost everything in the fire.
A deputy responds to a report of domestic abuse along with an assault with a deadly weapon; a traffic stop on a vehicle with an expired registration reveals three women who have some drug habits.
Deputies encounter a reported verbal disturbance outside an apartment complex; after searching the suspects they find heroin.
Deputies respond by boat to a report of an injured woman; a woman allegedly fights with a mother and her child; a 92-year-old man with dementia becomes lost.
Deputies respond to a burglar alarm at a hardware store; there's a call about drunk and disorderly people at a campground; an alarm goes off at a business park.
An intoxicated man runs through the streets in his underwear; a couple fights in their car; a couple won't stop fighting.
While patrolling an area after a string of recent burglaries, a deputy finds a wanted man; a deputy is alerted to the location of two men with drugs, firing off their guns.

A couple is caught having sex in a place where no one is supposed to be; a bag of highly explosive material is found attached to a mailbox; a drone spots a large marijuana growing site; a man puts his fist through a motel window.
Deputy Roberts shares his background and the reasons why he entered into law enforcement.
An undercover narcotics team goes after a known drug house; a man assaults his own father; a drunk motorist drives over a cliff and into a river.

The entire Sheriff's department engages in active school shooter training; a deputy sees through a string of lies after approaching a drug addict walking the streets at night; a transient verbally assaults pedestrians.
A dangerous fugitive is wanted for assault and battery; a deputy stops an unregistered vehicle; a look at the daily procedures deputies must follow before going on patrol.
The team leader of the Western El Dorado Narcotics Enforcement Team talks about the county's marijuana problem; the team takes down a hidden commercial marijuana grow house.
Following Deputy Bryan Payne on his night shift and seeing his skills to cover such a large area.

Police and rescue workers respond to a vehicle that collided with a tree; a car full of teens is pulled over; the investigation of a suspicious vehicle in a freeway parking area leads to the arrest of a gang member.

Officers respond to an ongoing fight between drug users in the Pollock Pines Hills; a deputy responds to a report of a drug overdose; a woman complains she is being harassed because she is of Mexican descent.

A deputy finds an overturned vehicle with an intoxicated driver inside; a foreign national from Guatemala is arrested for driving with a suspended license; a traffic stop leads to an arrest on a felony warrant; an intoxicated driver at a gas station.
An illegal marijuana grow operation is found in a mobile home; a deputy responds to a report of a loud and violent neighbor; a home burglary is interrupted by the homeowners.
An intoxicated young man exposes the dysfunctional mind of an alcoholic; a known drug user is found roaming a department store parking lot.
The Western El Dorado Narcotics Enforcement team plans and executes the raid of a large drug cartel; the team converges on the operation of a mid-level methamphetamine dealer.

A deputy responding to a call in the outlying area of the county finds a large illegal marijuana grow operation; the process of destroying illegal marijuana gardens; an officer investigates several reports of petty theft.
When a forest fire in California forces residents to evacuate, deputies assist by leading people and animals to safety.
A traffic stop leads to the arrest of a central figure in a major ID theft ring; a deputy answers a domestic violence call; a driver is arrested for warrants after a traffic stop.
Following a SWAT mission from briefing to execution; a man wanted for assault with a deadly weapon is taken into custody.
Deputies clear several illegal camped and hostile transient camp residents.

The Special Enforcement Detail prepares to take down a person with a felony warrant for theft and drug possession; deputies investigating a disturbance in a field discover minors in possession of drugs and alcohol.
S.E.D. and Probation Deputies pick up people with warrants of $150,000 or more.
Deputies respond to a burglary in progress; deputies do a probation check and find a houseful of drug addicts and probation violators.
Behind-the-scenes of the planning and execution of a large drug bust.
A father, worried about the behavior of his 15-year-old son, takes him to visit the El Dorado County Jail.
A deputy responds to a 911 call reporting a verbal argument between a man and a woman.
Deputies search for a man wanted for felonious assault and domestic violence; police make a traffic stop on a person they had arrested in the past.
After a deranged scientist steals the egg of a hybrid animal, members of a film crew run from the creature before the people become its dinner.

After a stint in the army, former male prostitute Sonny Phillips (James Franco) returns to his home in a run-down New Orleans in search of a stable life. However, the financial difficulties faced by his mother, Jewel (Brenda Blethyn), who is also a prostitute, make escaping his former life difficult. With few job prospects, Sonny reluctantly begins working the streets. The only bright spot in his otherwise difficult life is his relationship with Carol (Mena Suvari), Jewel's new protégé.
Life on Earth is rapidly destroyed except for a small area in Eastern Europe.
A half-shark, half-octopus battles a half-pterodactyl, half-barracuda.
In the 1930s, an effete Chicago mobster (Jose Ferrer) pits a Chinese kicker (Jackie Chan) against a king-size brute called Kiss.
Two men fight for survival after their plane crashes into the Pacific Ocean during the Battle of Midway.

Danny (Chris Pine) is a blind man who does not let his impairment get in the way of living his life to the fullest, except when it comes to love. Danny's brother (Eddie Kaye Thomas) sets him up on a series of blind dates, but all of them go disastrously wrong. Just when Danny is about to give up, he meets Leeza (Anjali Jay), a nurse who works for Danny's doctor. There is just one catch: Leeza, who is from India, is promised to another man.

Sarah (Elizabeth Olsen) is working with her father (Adam Trese) and uncle (Eric Sheffer Stevens) to renovate an old family home to prepare it for sale. Long vacant, the house has no utilities, forcing the trio to rely on battery-operated lanterns to light their way. Sarah becomes separated from her relatives and soon finds she is trapped inside the cabin, with no contact with the outside world. Panic turns to real terror as the young woman experiences events that become increasingly ominous.
Karloff introduces tales of a haunted nurse (Jacqueline Pierreux), a stalked call-girl (Michèle Mercier) and a vampire (Boris Karloff).

An angst-ridden London youth, Jimmy Cooper (Phil Daniels) escapes the drudgery of his postal job as a member of the Mods, a sharply dressed gang constantly at odds with their rivals, the Rockers. When the Mods and Rockers clash in the coastal town of Brighton, England, it leads to both trouble and an encounter with the lovely Steph (Leslie Ash). Returning to London, Jimmy, who aspires to be like Mod leader Ace Face (Sting), becomes even more disillusioned and longs to return to Brighton.
Lives change for members of an Irish family after a meteor crashes in their backyard.
A half-shark, half-octopus battles a hybrid of a killer whale and a wolf.
The UCOS team reinvestigate the murder of Eddie Chapman, leader of a notorious criminal motorbike gang, The Braves, when new evidence is brought to them by an unlikely source.
The team reinvestigates the murder of an unidentified male found in a West London alleyway seven years ago.
UCOS reopens the case of zookeeper Zac Halsey, who was found mauled to death in the tiger enclosure at Harefield Zoo in 2006.
The body of a woman is found on train tracks in London, badly damaged from electrical burns.
The search for Jenny's killer hits a wall, her friends at the women's refuge seek answers.
When a skeleton is found in concrete, the Lyell team must solve a case from 20 years ago.
The Lyell team identifies the concrete-encased remains as those of Derek Marshall; Clarissa traces payments to a cryogenics facility, leading to the discovery of another suspicious death.
Jack Halford announces that he's leaving UCOS; Stephen Fisher gives the team 24 hours to solve the murder of a woman dating back 100 years.
The UCOS team investigates the disappearance of a young PE teacher; the remains of the body are discovered in woodlands near a boarding school.
When UCOS reinvestigate the suspected suicide of a young diplomat, DS Sandra Pullman breaks the rules to explore a possible cover-up at the Foreign Office.
The team's feathers are ruffled when Steve McAndrew, a retired detective from Glasgow, joins the team to reinvestigate an old case.
When the body of missing computer expert Martin Longthorn turns up in a hospital morgue under a false name, the team members find themselves drawn into the unfamiliar world of online hacking.
The team investigates the death of a 16-year-old tennis star who fell - or was pushed - from a penthouse balcony after she lost an important match to a rival.
The team re-opens the case of a talented young poet whose burnt body is discovered in the scrapyard of a known gangster after ten years.

UCOS investigate the murder of Max Klein, an East German immigrant whose mysterious last words translated as 'blue flower'. As the team piece together Max's remarkable story, Pullman attempts to gain the trust of his estranged daughter Mia.

Standing and McAndrew travel to Glasgow, where a new UCOS section is being established; they agree to help investigate the unsolved murder of a bookie called James Soutar; the case brings McAndrew face-to-face with an old adversary.
Standing and McAndrew travel to Glasgow, where a new UCOS section is being established; they agree to help investigate the unsolved murder of a bookie called James Soutar.
Bored, Walt quizzes the guys on comic book trivia; a customer sells a Hellboy prop replica.
The Stash helps auction off the work of Mike Esposito; Walt buys a paper doll.
The guys have the opportunity to buy a replica of the '66 Batcycle; a collection of Marvel fan magazines from the '70s.
A young man wants to appraise his collection; Walt buys Wayne Gretzky memorabilia.
Jason Mewes invites the guys to a Renaissance fair; a customer brings in a valuable item.
Kevin Smith sends his daughter to The Stash to learn how to be a clerk; a customer wants to sell rare and unusual "Rocky" action figures.
A returning customer brings in a toy that Walt always coveted; an aspiring student brings in an autographed book.
Walt challenges the others to perform stand-up routines; a collector brings in Marvel Comics from the 1960s.
The guys agree to baby-sit a friend's daughter for the afternoon; an Indiana Jones superfan has items from the films.
Walt and the others attend BronyCon, a convention for "My Little Pony" fans; a customer wants to sell a Godzilla board game from the 1970s.
Walt considers buying the hand and footprints of Adam West and Burt Ward; a rare set of Star Wars comic strips.
The co-creator of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Kevin Eastman, brings in early sketches of the turtles.
Walt has a business proposition for original Ghostbuster, Ernie Hudson; a customer wants to sell cartoon shampoo bottles from the 1960s.
Adam West visits and a race between the Batmobile and Black Beauty ensues; a customer sells the first appearance of Rocket Raccoon.
Artist Neal Adams and writer Denny O'Neil visit the Stash; the guys see a set of 50-year-old Batman night lights.
Butch Patrick (Eddie Munster) stops by the Stash; a never officially released rare Star Wars action figure.
Kevin's assistant, Ashley, learns about comic book retail at the Stash; pro wrestlers want to sell their comic.
Darryl McDaniels of Run-DMC brings his new comic to the Stash; the guys look at a Marvel Silver Age number one issue.
Billy Dee Williams stops by the store to win the Millennium Falcon the same way Lando lost it: a high-stakes card game.
Jason Mewes hangs out and plays clerk at the Stash; Walt wants to acquire a mysterious recreation of comic book art.
The guys attend a KISS concert; Walt lives out his childhood dream of meeting Gene Simmons; Ming considers buying an arcade cabinet.
Peter Mayhew ("Chewbacca") judges a Wookiee contest at the Stash; one of the hottest comic books of the 1990s.
Mike flies in the Batcopter to celebrate fifteen years at the Secret Stash; the guys look at one of the hottest books of the '90s.
Kevin talks comics with actor William Shatner; Walt covets a Mego doll that has unique packaging.
The guys and Bryan visit a "Jaws" museum; super-powered toilet paper comes through.
The guys are prompted to reconsider their preparations for the apocalypse by a zombie comic; an eccentric collector wants Walt's help.
Stan Lee helps a customer who is experiencing a comics crisis; a customer buys a classic issue of Fantastic Four.
Secret Stash employees audition with Walt and Bryan for a role in the claymation film they are making with Brian Quinn.
Comics artist, John Romita, Jr., draws an original piece for the Stash; Bryan shows interest in an Evel Knievel toy from his childhood.
Inspired by an old friend, the guys wear cowboy hats, and celebrate the old Wild West; a customer is searching for an iconic comic from the '80s.
Artist Jim Lee shares tales from the world of comics on the podcast; a comic book brings wedding bells to the Stash.
When Ming gets a selfie stick, he tries to go viral by filming the Stash; Walt examines bootleg toys of an '80s blockbuster.
Jason Mewes brings his infant daughter to the Stash to meet everyone; a customer sells comic book Slurpee cups.
Real-life superhero, Phoenix Jones, visits the store and patrols Red Bank with the guys; Walt reminisces about a Batman playset.
Walt and the boys go on a trip to cross off a bucket-list item; four key Spider-Man issues come to the Stash.
The Stash sponsors a blood drive at the shop with the help of horror queen Elvira; the boys discuss the joys of "Mystery Science Theater 3000."
When a vintage 1980s Pac-Man game lands on the counter, Ming prepares for battle; a rare Beatles board game excites the guys.
KITT from "Knight Rider" pulls up to the Stash; a rare Green Arrow Mego figure and Archie Bunker's grandson.
Lindsay Wagner ("The Bionic Woman") stops in for a Silver Surfer item; Jem and Ghostbusters toys spark another round of banter.
Ming and a customer joust over the price of Batman 111; Wolverine becomes the largest statue to ever enter the Stash.
Kevin and Harley visit for the Yoga Hosers premiere; Ming becomes a lead villain with help from a special-effects makeup legend.
Members of the 501st Legion of Stormtroopers invade the Stash looking for new recruits; the fate of a vintage Ewok playset.
Ralph Macchio seeks a rare "Karate Kid" playset; Ming gets an unforgettable lesson; Walt gets excited about a Mechagodzilla.
The guys prepare for a maritime adventure when the Batboat docks in Red Bank; Batman's first appearance.
Jason Mewes inserts himself into transactions involving a Deadshot statue and a vintage Death Star Space Station.
Actress Katrina Law ("Arrow") wants a copy of Batman 232; old school items involving Popeye, Dynomutt and Pogs.
Walt steps into the ring with a customer over an original Rock 'Em Sock 'Em Robots game; a rare piece of original Sal Buscema art.
Marky Ramone shares his artwork and bonds with Walt over robots; a King Kong item from 1975.
A Kreskin ESP game reveals Walt's powers of cognition; discussions about Mork from Ork and Dick Tracy's Rogues' Gallery.
Tom Cavanaugh visits the shop; Walt finds a Golden Age classic with "Human Torch No. 2."
Kevin Smith and the guys discuss how "The Walking Dead" started out as a comic book and became a cultural phenomenon.
Legendary horror icon Robert Englund, aka Freddy Krueger, personally delivers a birthday present to Ming.
The Stash & Red Bank cosplayers celebrate the centennial of Jack Kirby; one of the greatest innovators in comic book history.
Influential actor and rapper Method Man talks to the guys about his extensive comic book collection; "Starsky & Hutch" gear takes over The Stash.
Jay & Silent Bob cosplayers take over the streets of Red Bank; the Comic Book Men attempt to make history by setting a Guinness World Record.
Rare and interesting Star Wars items making their way into the Stash; Walt offers up big cash to try and score a beacon for the store.
Kevin Smith and the guys attend the premiere screening of a movie about themselves and the origination of the film "Clerks."
Actor Burt Ward, best known for portraying television's famous Robin the Boy Wonder, reminisces about his time on the set of "Batman" and judges the Stash's canine cosplay contest.
Walt meets his match during a heated negotiation with actor Mike Colter ("Luke Cage"); a "legendary" video game becomes both Walt's trash and Ming's treasure.
Troma Entertainment co-founder Lloyd Kaufman and his crew put the guys through a grueling audition to see if they have what it takes to be in a Troma film.
Adriano Zumbo puts 12 amateur dessert makers to the test; contestants must make a dessert that best reflects them.
The amateur cooks are tasked with bringing a "Franken-Zumbo" to life.
Following a chocolate-themed challenge, two contestants face a Zumbo Test involving 100 handmade profiteroles.

Chuck travels to Mashteuiatsh to meet Frederick Raphaël and his son Charlie, both avid hunters; together, they drive to the family's chalet in Ashuapmushuan, where they practice one of their favorite wildlife activities: hunting and field dressing.
Kirsten demonstrates her unique version of a chocolate toastie, a common household snack; she also provides a recipe for a banana split, which she describes as the ultimate version of the dish.
Kirsten puts her very own twist on some simple show-stopping chocolate pieces and makes them extra eye-catching.

Holiday bakers compete in a quick elimination round with hot chocolate as the mystery ingredient; the final two bakers compete for $10,000 and a spot in the Holiday Championship Finale with a winter wonderland-themed pie showdown.

One home baker tries to go with the flow with a lava cake; Chef Lynn Crawford hits a sweet spot with the Meyer lemons and honey in her pantry; it's an all-out cookie war to see who take home the prize.
Renowned pastry chef, master chocolatier and entrepreneur Steve Hodge works with beloved design guru Tiffany Pratt.
After 10 years in business, Lesley and her partner Jordan struggle to find work-life balance at OMG Baked Goodness in Toronto.
Pastry chef and chocolatier Kirsten Tibballs provides a number of handy tips and tricks for superior home baking.
Lentils are a popular Saskatchewan crop that's often shipped overseas; a farmer, a brewer and a chef are changing that.
Jenn visits an organic grain farmer, a baker and a whiskey maker to learn about the various uses of wheat.

Sarah visits a local walnut farm and nut oil press, using these versatile nuts to make a walnut ravioli in a cream sauce, a rolled leg of lamb with walnut and arugula stuffing, and a walnut tart with butterscotch sauce.

Sarah visits a traditional mushroom festival in France; gets put to work at her local cheese maker; prepares a date night menu that includes a cream of Cepe mushroom soup, a Provence-inspired roast chicken with lemon, artichoke and peppers.
On the menu are flashy fish stew, saffron sauce and garlic bread, plus seared Asian beef, and a noodle salad with ginger dressing.
Jamie prepares two delicious, nutritious, fast family meals back-to-back: chili con carne meatballs, and sticky kicking chicken with a watermelon radish salad and crunchy noodles.
Mena restaurant-hops with friends Lilly Singh and Laura Marano, indulging in plant-based French pastries, "pastrami" sammies, Thai "chicken" wings and "carne" asada.
From a sumptuous meringue with blackcurrant coulis, to a heritage salad with beetroot straight from his gardens, there's something for every palate.
Anna demonstrates how to make American, Italian and Belgian-style waffles.
Anna prepares three of her favorite muffin recipes, ranging from simple and healthy to decadent.

Roto Rooter is the largest plumbing and drain cleaning business in North America. President and CEO Rick Arquilla wants to take his company from good to great, but as he struggles to use systems he designed, fights to overcome his fear of rats and bungles a welding job, he realises he has more to learn from his employees than he could ever teach them.
Uzzi covers Daniel's top-shelf blunder and Pash loses Jayson's fast-food fail. Meanwhile, Sketch celebrates Grandad Pete's life of grime and Alice erases Jemma's dire dating days.

The Tattoo Fixers come to the aid of Patrice, whose tattoo portrait of her dearly departed grandmother ended up looking like a well-known Corrie star. Cheeky Michael needs help with a holiday tattoo that's writing cheques his anatomy can't cash.
Visitors to the studio include Luke, whose tribute to his beloved mum went drastically wrong. Meanwhile, Sketch helps Sian cover a clown tattoo that's scaring the life out of anyone who sees it.
Eccentric dancer Marina wants a confidence-boosting tattoo cover to get her back onto the podium. The artists see double when identical twins Hayley and Rebecca come in with matching bad body art.

The team meet Brix, who is a transgender person, and wants to cover his feminine tattoo with a more masculine one. Lou helps out tomboy Lucy, who has come in with a vulgar phrase tattooed on her leg that amuses the boys but repulses the girls.
Ramsay visits Moore Place in Esher where joint owners Nick Whitehouse and Richard Hodgson are trying to create a profitable business with a complete lack of know-how in the kitchen.

The venue for this programme is La Lanterna in Letchworth, Hertfordshire. Twenty-eight-year-old owner and head chef Alex offers modern Italian cuisine, a taste of Little Italy in England's first garden city, and the restaurant is run by his best mate maître d' Gavin, helped by his ex-air hostess girlfriend Emily.

The venue for this edition is D-Place in Chelmsford, run by Mexican-born Israel and his English partner Tara. They've sunk £150,000 of their own money into their trendy café bar, which offers a vast selection of fusion cuisine. In charge is executive chef Philippe, producing everything from all-day breakfasts to Hoisin noodles with an astounding lack of flair.

The venue for this edition is Momma Cherri's Soul Food Shack, an intimate 40-seater a stone's throw from Brighton's sea front. Owner Charita Jones produces a menu of irresistibly unique classics from the Deep South.

The venue for the fourth programme is La Riviera, a fine dining restaurant in Inverness. Owned by multi-millionaire Barry Larson and costing £8,000 a week to run, the place boasts top French chef Loïc Lefebvre and an impeccably-trained kitchen staff with Michelin star-studded backgrounds. Loïc is on a mission to bring sophisticated French cooking to the home of haggis, tatties and deep-fried Mars bars.

Clubway 41 in Blackpool is a 40-seater restaurant above a café, both owned and run by David Jackson and his partner Dawn Brindley. Despite being voted Blackpool Tourist Board's Restaurant of the Year, Clubway 41 is in dire straits. David and Dawn are breaking all the cardinal rules for running a successful food business; in fact, there are no rules, and it shows.
This episode's venue is Irish family-run restaurant Oscars in Nantwich, Cheshire, run by Maura - who also heads up the front-of-house team - and her son and head chef Lenin.

The venue for this programme is Sandgate in Kent, where husband and wife team Lois and Peter Hamilton-Slade own and run a small English seaside hotel. They enjoy eating in restaurants and thought it would be fun to own one, so they pooled their life savings with no previous experience in the industry. Here, there's chaos in the kitchen as first-time head chef Stuart struggles with the demands of each menu.

The programme visits La Gondola in Derby, a hotel and restaurant owned and run by businesswoman Daniela Bayfield. In the past La Gondola was the toast of Derby, reaching the height of its reputation in the 1970s and early 1980s, but the glory days are long gone, and La Gondola is sinking fast. The restaurant's decor, staff and food are all stuck in the past.

Gordon Ramsay is sharpening his knives - and his tongue - for another assault on some of the country's scariest restaurant kitchens. Gordon takes on a restaurant abroad. La Parra de Burriana is an ex-pat restaurant in Nerja on Spain's Costa del Sol. Nestling among the cafés lining the seafront offering all-day English breakfast and chips, La Parra is the brainchild of 26-year-old ex-nightclub manager Laurence.

Gordon tackles a pub for the first time, getting to grips with The Fenwick Arms in rural Lancashire. The pub is run by landlord Brian who, after 30 years in the business and a quadruple heart-bypass, still puts in 120 hours a week and insists on laying down the law in the kitchen. Despite their best endeavours Brian and his partner Elaine are £250,000 in debt, and are losing £1,500 a week.

For the last three years Morgan's has been run by antiques dealer-turned-restaurateur Sandy and her daughters Helen and Laura. The beautifully-designed dining room has a prime high street location and should be the perfect eatery for the trendy local clientele, but head chef Phil is grappling with an eclectic menu that includes mashed potato with apricots, and his cooking's just not up to it. Can Gordon help?

For the last 18 months ex Michelin-starred chef Nick has owned and run Rococo, but his past success is now eluding him. The menu is past its sell-by date, the service is stuffy, the food is over-priced and the only thing being fed is his ego. With debts of £100k, Gordon forces him to face his failures, strips down the menu and dismantles the claustrophobic dining room.

Gordon Ramsay is back with his trademark mix of tough talking and inspirational leadership for another foray into some of the country's scariest kitchens. The venue is Ruby Tate's in Brighton, owned and run by ex-actor and failed Hollywood wannabe Allan Love. It's an oyster bar and seafood restaurant, but Allan's never tasted the food because he hates fish. Can Gordon persuade Allan to shape up?

Gordon takes on The Priory, a 100-seater carvery in Haywards Heath, Sussex. It's owned by ex-IT consultant Scott and located in a beautiful former convent, offering bargain roast dinners. Scott bought the place for £300,000, but with an ageing clientele eating for half price, he's losing £5,000 a week. Despite the heavenly location, the food is straight from hell.

Piccolo Teatro is a bijou vegetarian restaurant in Paris run by feisty Scot Rachel. A former waitress at the restaurant, Rachel bought it three years ago and now, along with best friend Stephanie, she's trying to convert the carnivorous French into a nation of veggies. For Gordon, his trip to Piccolo Teatro turns into one of his biggest nightmares yet. Will he be able to perform a miracle, or admit defeat?

The Curry Lounge in Nottingham is a 120-seater Indian restaurant which has been run since January 2007 by ex-sales director Raz, who's new to the business, and it shows. Despite a £500,000 refurbishment and decor like a Bollywood set, the honeymoon period's well and truly over. Enter Gordon, relishing the prospect of tackling an Indian restaurant for the first time.

The Granary in rural Hampshire is an upmarket restaurant, which at 200 seats, is the biggest Gordon's ever taken on. Originally opened by entrepreneur Nigel Nieddu as an upmarket dining club four years ago, the restaurant was relaunched after a £2 million refit, but it's still losing £4,000 a week. It promises classy modern British cuisine but in reality the menu features food sourced from all over the globe.

Gordon visits the Fish & Anchor, a restaurant and bar near Lampeter in rural West Wales, owned and run by ex-boxer Mike and his wife Caron. Mike, a self-taught cook, is a one-man pressure cooker in the kitchen as he struggles to accommodate a vast menu, while Caron's unique style of front-of-house management includes abusing the customers and her husband in equal measure.
Gordon attempts to help two friends save their failing tapas bar and nightclub from corporate competition.
Gordon attempts to help turn around a family-run bistro with hideous decor, bad food and a chef who can't face up to his mistakes.
Gordon Ramsay visits Mayfair, a restaurant in a prime location on the busy seafront in Fuengirola, on the Costa del Sol. The restaurant was set up 28 years ago by Londoner Pat and her husband Jack.
Sonic and Tails team up in an attempt to thwart Robotnik's scheme to possess the magical Deep Power Stones.
The Hedgehogs steal historical objects of Mobius from Robotnik before he can hock them off at an auction.
A group of Freedom Fighters is obliterated by a swarm of metallic fly-bots; when Manic goes looking for the insects, he is stung with serum.
A speed enhancing fluid deemed Sonic Tonic is created by Robotnik to make him as fast as Sonic so that he may finally catch him.
The Hedgehogs congregate on the Floating Island in their latest effort to find their mother; Sleet and Dingo also have an interest on this island.
As Sonic begins to chow chili dogs for a snack, he finds a message in the sack from his mother urging him to head to Speedster Island.
Sonic becomes aggravated that maybe their efforts of fighting for freedom seem pointless. Sonia suggests that they go to the Oracle for advice.
Robotnik has his eyes set upon Queen Aleena's crown jewel, but Sonic, Manic and Sonia plan to retrieve the gem before Robotnik.
Sonic, Manic and Sonia find an abandoned baby in an alley and begin to look for the baby's parents. Manic becomes very fond of the child.
Robotnik makes an announcement that he and Queen Aleena will be wed so he can become king of Mobius.
Robotnik's doomsday project begins a week earlier than anyone had anticipated; the Freedom Fighters prepare for what may be their final battle.
Princess Sally and Antoine follow up on a lead that suggests her father, King Acorn, may be alive; Sonic attempts to rescue a captured Freedom Fighter.
Sally is taken prisoner by Robotnik and Snively, who construct a robotized Sally clone.
Sonic and the Freedom Fighters travel to Robotnik's lab hoping to decipher his Roboticizer system.
Sonic and the Freedom Fighters look for the secret scrolls that have great powers.
Sonic and Sally encounter the Guardian while on a mission to the big city to replace Nicole's malfunctioning microchip.

While on a mission to the big city to replace Nicole's malfunctioning microchip, Sonic and Sally encounter the Guardian, a mysterious cloaked figure who guards a dormant wizard named Lazar and his computer of evil spells.
Sonic conquers a vehicle designed to locate and destroy living tissue matter during a solo mission to the Badlands.
A captain of the Queen's guard is captured before he can reach the secret rendezvous where he was to meet Queen Aleena.
A homecoming is interrupted for Sonic, Sonia and Manic when Sleet and Dingo arrive to collect back taxes after returning to their birthplace.
Sonia discovers that the watch she received from her friend is actually a monitoring device for the Robotnik Intelligence Agency.
Sleet and Dingo plan to collect the taxes owed to Robotnik from the Duke of Velcronia but keep it for themselves.
Robotnik blackmails Cyrus by kidnapping his father and holding him hostage.
On a trip to Port Mobius, Sonic, Manic and Sonia are told that ships are sinking due to the Mobian sea-beast.
Rumor has it that Queen Aleena's journals are buried in the city of Tashistan; Sonic and his siblings search the city for the scrolls.

Comedian and stage actress Carol Burnett, who first gained popularity during her stint on "The Gary Moore Show," hosted this one-hour variety series. Her talented supporting players included Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, Vicki Lawrence (who got the job based on her resemblance to Burnett) and Lyle Waggoner. Skits often featured guest stars, such as Mama Cass of the Mamas and the Papas or singer Steve Lawrence. One sketch, "The Family" (which featured Lawrence as the persnickety Mama and Burnett as her hotheaded daughter) was later spun-off into it's own sitcom.

Rick accede a dejar salir de sus celdas a los prisioneros si les ayudan a matar a los zombis que quedan en la prisión. Entretanto, la salud de Hershel empeora por momentos.

Andrea y Michonne descubren una comunidad de sobrevivientes liderada por un hombre llamado el Gobernador. Allá les ofrecen medicinas, comida, agua caliente y ropa limpia, pero Michonne desconfía del Gobernador y sus verdaderas intenciones.

En Woodbury, Michonne desconfía del Gobernador y planea irse sin Andrea. En la prisión, un sabotaje provoca que una horda de zombis penetre en la cárcel y, mientras Rick y sus compañeros los combaten, Lori entra en trabajo de parto.

Rick está totalmente abatido por la muerte de Lori, pero recibe una llamada telefónica sorprendente. Entretanto, Michonne ha descubierto el secreto del Gobernador y se dispone a abandonar Woodbury, a pesar de que Andrea quiere permanecer allá.

Michonne ve a Glenn y Maggie buscando provisiones, pero alguien más los observa: Merle, quien reconoce a Glenn como uno de los que le abandonó, a merced de los zombis, en una azotea de Atlanta. Entretanto, Rick sigue mentalmente inestable.
Michonne conduce a Rick, Daryl y Oscar a Woodbury para rescatar a Glenn y Maggie, a quienes el Gobernador está torturando para sonsacarles dónde se oculta el grupo de Rick.

El grupo de Rick invade Woodbury con la intención de rescatar a Glenn y Maggie. Michonne descubre el secreto familiar que oculta el Gobernador cuando trata de asesinarlo. En la prisión, un grupo desconocido atraviesa la verja de seguridad.
Rick y Maggie regresan a Woodbury para salvar a Daryl, quien está obligado a luchar contra su hermano. Entretanto, en la prisión, el grupo de Rick se encuentra con el grupo de Sasha y Tyreese.
En secreto, el Gobernador y sus hombres preparan una incursión mortal contra la prisión. Darryl y Merle llegan en mitad de la contienda.

El Gobernador permite a Andrea, acompañada de Milton, ir a la prisión a negociar la paz con su antiguo grupo. Mientras, Tyreese y Sasha llegan a Woodbury y le ofrecen al Gobernador información sobre la prisión a cambio de poder quedarse allá.
Rick, Michonne y Carl viajan al condado de Rick en busca de armamento y encuentran a alguien a quien creían muerto. Durante la misión, Rick cambia la percepción que tiene de Michonne.
Andrea concierta un encuentro entre Rick y el Gobernador para que negocien la paz, pero el Gobernador exige la cabeza de Michonne a cambio del alto el fuego.

Andrea descubre la verdad sobre el Gobernador e intenta huir para alertar al grupo de Rick, pero el Gobernador envía a sus hombres en su busca. Entretanto, alguien ha provocado un sabotaje en Woodbury y los sospechosos son Tyreese y Milton.
Rick duda entre entregarle o no a Michonne al Gobernador y poner así fin a la contienda. Sin embargo, Merle se anticipa a las órdenes de Rick y decide tomar una decisión por su propia cuenta.
El Gobernador y sus hombres lanzan un ataque contra la prisión, pero el grupo de Rick se defiende. Al final de la contienda, solo una de las dos comunidades podrá seguir existiendo.

Fresh out of prison for car theft, Dick Kanipsia (James Caan) goes to visit a fellow ex-con, Harry Moss (Richard B. Shull), and arrives just in time to see him gunned down by faceless assassins. Vincent Parry (Humphrey Bogart) has just escaped from prison after being locked up for a crime he did not commit -- murdering his wife. After getting a ride out of town from a stranger, Vincent crosses paths with a young woman (Lauren Bacall) who lets him stay in her apartment while he heals and continues to try and clear his name.

Guy Gabaldon is an orphaned Latino youth raised in Los Angeles by an adoptive Japanese-American family. With the dawn of conflict in the Pacific, Gabaldon enlists in the military as a translator. Fighting in the Battle of Saipan, he's horrified at the carnage. So, disobeying orders, he goes behind enemy lines and talks the Japanese into willful surrender, saving thousands of lives on both sides. The film is based on the true story of the decorated World War II veteran.

After eloping, the young lovers embark on an armed robbery spree, managing to elude the authorities until Annie insists on pulling one last job.

However, when she hears that gold-digging Crystal is making Steve unhappy, Kay resolves to get her husband back.

A jury convicts Kara Garvin for the brutal murder of three members of the Mollett family in their rural Ohio trailer; Kara's mother and sister say she's incapable of violence.

A jury convicts a woman of murdering her husband as he lied in bed; her children insist that his death was actually a suicide, and they reach out to Chris and Fatima to get to the truth.

Chris Anderson and Fatima Silva hear the case of Joel Atkin, a man who made a wrong turn in 2009, sparking a petty argument that left one man dead and Atkin in prison for murder.

After a robbery gone bad, a jury convicts Garrett Arrowood of killing his aunt; his mother and sister say two con men made him their mark, and now he sits in prison; Chris Anderson and Fatima Silva dig deep to prove his innocence or reveal his guilt.

Chris and Fatima investigate the case of Patricia Rorrer, who is in prison for brutally murdering her former boyfriend's wife and baby out of spite; her lawyers claim that she was not in the same state at the time of the crime.

Eric Miller was a small-time pot dealer convicted of killing a friend for $60 in cash. His girlfriend and daughter believe the system locked away the wrong man. They're hoping Chris and Fatima will join their fight to free Eric Miller.

A disabled man dies three weeks after a brutal beating for his TV and VCR; a jury sentences three people to life in prison based on the testimony of just one woman, but she may not be telling the truth; Chris and Fatima investigate.

Forensics shows the real killer in the murder of a socialite on Valentine's Day 2001.
The disappearance of millionaire Frank Black.

In fall 1991, Toronto was paralyzed by the story of a missing six-year-old girl found raped and murdered in the boiler room of her apartment building; with four suspects, CSIs turned to the brand-new science of DNA to catch the killer.
In 1990, Gainesville, Fla., becomes the site of a number of coed murders.
Explosive experts sifting through bomb evidence discover a more insidious plan.
An abandoned suitcase containing a young woman's body, leads to a mystery of a second woman missing too.
The murder of a gay couple in rural California leads investigators into the world of hate crimes.
Investigators are drawn into the dark world of high-end prostitution, illegal aliens and Russian organized crime.

A woman's lively get-together at her local bar ends with a baffling murder.

Twenty-year-old single mother Tracy Whitehead is starting to turn her life around when she falls for attentive Joby Palczynzki, then his jealousy starts to overtake their relationship, and she soon comes to realize she can run, but she can't hide.
